Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has sought a comprehensive partnership with China Harbour Engineering Company Limited for the development of the proposed Abia Seaport City. Otti said the state preferred an arrangement that would involve the Chinese firm in the project’s feasibility studies, construction and eventual delivery rather than limiting its participation to consultancy services. The governor spoke on Monday while receiving a delegation led by CHEC’s Managing Director, Wang Jason, who presented preliminary findings and proposals for the project. He stressed that the state was interested in receiving honest and professional advice based on the company’s findings, noting that the feasibility study would determine the project’s viability and appropriate technical direction. “I am sure that my people will be engaging with you. But I know they need some clarifications. “So, my preference would have been a partnership that takes off from the feasibility, to the construction and ultimately delivery,” Otti said. The governor described the proposed arrangement as a genuine public-private partnership, assuring the Chinese firm that his administration was committed to transparency, integrity and mutually beneficial business relationships. “So in that case, it’s a real public-private partnership transaction. The major things you have said are also what we believe in. We don’t play games, we don’t cheat people. “So, if you are in partnership with us, you can be sure that you can go to bed and sleep,” he added. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. He disclosed that the state had also attracted interest from other prospective investors, including Afreximbank, whose participation would equally depend on the outcome of the feasibility study. The governor said his administration was prepared to support the project and work with the company to ensure its successful implementation. He, however, noted that the development would require patience, strategic planning, technical capacity and long-term commitment. He expressed optimism that the project, when integrated with other infrastructure and economic activities, could significantly transform Abia’s economic landscape. Otti further said his administration’s development agenda was anchored on a long-term framework, noting that the state had enacted a 25-year development plan into law to ensure continuity in governance and development projects beyond successive administrations. Earlier, Jason described the proposed seaport project as viable and capable of contributing significantly to the development of the state. The only thing we need to verify is what kind of port or what depth will be more viable. That doesn’t mean we don’t have an available option. “We need to use a feasibility study to find out the most viable, most suitable solution for this area. So, that’s the reason. Generally, if I don’t believe this one is possible anyway, I won’t want to be involved,” he said. Jason said CHEC had considerable expertise in feasibility studies and port infrastructure development but was more interested in establishing a long-term relationship with Abia State than undertaking consultancy work alone. “Certainly, for China Harbour, this feasibility study, we are good at it; it is our major business, and we have to do a good job. But we are not focused on this, on the consultancy work. We wish to have a long-term cooperation with Abia State for the future development and delivery. “But for the detailed cooperation model, the business model, I think after the feasibility study, we can continue the discussion. I think it will be more serious for me to express our position,” Jason stated. He said he was impressed by Aba’s economic significance, describing the commercial city as an important hub in Nigeria and expressing confidence in its potential to support the proposed integrated infrastructure development. The proposed seaport is part of Abia State’s plan to improve maritime access for the South-East and strengthen the region’s trade and logistics capacity. The project, identified as the Azumini–Obeaku Seaport and Inland Waterways Corridor, is located in the Azumini area of Ukwa East Local Government Area. The proposed port is expected to provide a maritime gateway for Aba’s industrial and commercial activities and potentially reduce the cost of transporting goods for manufacturers in the region. It could also create a logistics corridor linking the South-East to international markets. Otti had earlier approved a feasibility study for the project in May 2026, directing CHEC to accelerate the process. The study is expected to establish the technical, economic and environmental requirements, including the dredging needed to make the proposed waterway navigable. Its findings will help determine whether the project is viable and the appropriate investment and construction model. The governor was accompanied at Monday’s meeting by the Secretary to the State Government, Dr Emmanuel Meribeole, and other members of the State Executive Council.
